**Visual analysis of the test image:**

- **Plant**: Wheat (*Triticum aestivum*)
- **Affected part**: Leaf blade
- **Key features**:
  - Broad, prominent **yellow/cream-colored stripes** running the full length of the leaf, parallel to the veins
  - Alternating yellow and green bands creating a striped mosaic appearance
  - No visible pustules or spore masses (rules out rust diseases)
  - Clean stripe margins — not blotchy or water-soaked (rules out bacterial streak)
  - The yellowing is chlorotic (not necrotic)

**Differential reasoning:**

| Disease | Match |
|---|---|
| **Wheat_Streak_Mosaic_Virus** | Strong — causes elongated chlorotic streaks/mosaic parallel to veins in wheat |
| Cephalosporium_Stripe | Moderate — also causes vein-parallel stripes, but usually narrower and follows single vascular bundles |
| Stripe_Rust | Ruled out — no urediniospore pustules visible |
| Barley_Yellow_Dwarf_Virus | Ruled out — typically causes tip/marginal yellowing, not stripe pattern |
| Bacterial_Leaf_Streak | Ruled out — causes water-soaked tan/brown lesions, not chlorotic stripes |

The broad, elongated yellow-green chlorotic streaks running parallel to the veins — creating an alternating yellow/green mosaic pattern — are the hallmark of **Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus**. The virus disrupts chloroplast development along interveinal tissue, producing these characteristic vein-parallel chlorotic streaks.
